<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, touching **21** documentable anchor(s).

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `699afe9bb9222379d8760ac98ddeb476780e351b` — the merge of head `661fbd90d018703958917f7fea8484e6a5e1ba25` into base `ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 699afe9bb9222379d8760ac98ddeb476780e351b && git checkout 699afe9bb9222379d8760ac98ddeb476780e351b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e 661fbd90d018703958917f7fea8484e6a5e1ba25 && git checkout -B drift-repro ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e && git merge --no-ff 661fbd90d018703958917f7fea8484e6a5e1ba25

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ac8fede8f938439d2228f5b1404042d113a3812e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Green include Test Core 1-8/8, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check source and consumer gates, Lint and Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Check Changeset (both), Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards and the Dogfood Regression Gate aggregate.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes (author-time door, `os validate` / `os build`, `packages[]` artifacts only):

1. **A field's `picklist` held only by a sibling the declaring package does not reach through its declared closure, the declaring package having no dependency outside the artifact: was accepted, now refused** as `picklist-reference-unknown` (exit 1), the message being R's `outside-closure` sentence verbatim. **Right.** It is the runtime's verdict since E6: the boot warns and serves no options (ruling N2), and the post-seal install judge refuses (`plugin.ts`, `picklistReferenceVerdict(ref.picklist, caller, ordered)`). ADR-0150 D3 plus ruling N1 (6729820123: "a sibling package in the same release artifact is NOT in a package's resolution closure unless its manifest declares the dependency") is the rule.
2. **The same reference when the declaring package also depends on a package the artifact does not carry: was silent, now an `info` notice** (`picklist-reference-unverified`, never gating). **Right**: an outside dependency X can hold the name (then X is the unique holder in the closure) or depend on the sibling, so the door cannot prove the refusal.
3. **A field whose declaring package's closure reaches two holders (it declares both siblings), no outside dependency: was accepted, now refused** (`ambiguous-in-closure`, R's sentence; hint "Keep 'X' in one of ..."). **Right in substance**: D3 says verbatim "A reference that would resolve to two holders in P's closure is refused at `defineStack`, `os validate` and the save door", and the boot refuses it (`findUnresolvedPicklistReferences`: "one the closure holds more than once, still refuses the boot"). **Undeclared and unpinned** (④ F2).
4. **A `picklistExtensions[].extend` whose target two packages of the stack hold: was accepted, now refused** (`ambiguous-in-environment`, caller-less). **Right in substance**: the boot's `findOrphanPicklistExtensions` judges the target caller-less and refuses an ambiguity. **Undeclared and unpinned** (④ F2). The changeset's "A `picklistExtensions` entry's `extend` still resolves against any package of the stack" is true only for a target one package holds.
5. **The ambiguity arms (3 and 4) when the declaring package has an outside dependency: were silent, now an `info` notice** ("is held by each of ... — not judged", hint "If one of those packages declares 'X', nothing is wrong"). **Wrong**: an outside package can only add a holder, never remove one, so the runtime refuses this reference whatever the outside dependency holds (and the boot refuses it outright). The notice says the reference may be fine when it cannot be (④ F1).
6. **Unchanged:** a single-package stack (one body, every holder is the caller, step 1); a declared sibling (step 2); a transitive sibling through a declared sibling; a `sys`-namespace sibling (`kernelPackages`); the declaring package's own list (step 1 wins over any sibling); a name nothing holds (`not-found` keeps the old wording and the old refused-or-reported split); an extension of a list one sibling holds, with no dependency (ruling X, caller-less unique holder).

Is the door now exactly the runtime's resolver, with no second closure walk? **Yes for the rule and the closure.** `referenceResolver` calls `resolvePackageScopedHolders` with `packageResolutionClosure(registry, caller)`, the same two calls `resolvePackageScopedName` makes (`objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts:144-153`). `artifactRegistry` is a registry view (`getPackage` / `getAllPackages` over the bodies), the same shape as the install judge's `withPendingManifests`; it walks nothing itself. The App-pair widening (`widenPairClosureToAppMembers`) and the `sys` add-in come along for free. Two residual differences, both outside the rule. (a) The holder set is the door's own `picklistNamesOf(body)`, not the runtime's `collectManifestPicklistNames`, which also reads nested `plugins[]`. That predates this PR and is unchanged (N7). (b) The view omits `residualOwnerDependenciesOf`, so a body that declares the stack's own id as a dependency is walked no further there. Such a body has that id in `outside` anyway, so the result is a notice, never a false refusal.

Do the refusal sentence and the boot refusal agree? **Yes, for one holder, pinned on a real kernel.** The door's `message` is `verdict.message`, and the boot warning carries `${ref.refusal}`, the same `packageScopedRefusalMessage` over the same query. The new boot-parity describe asserts `[['status', door[0].message]]` equals `findOutsideClosurePicklistReferences()`. For two holders the candidate order is body order at the door and registration (hydrate) order at the boot, so the two sentences can name the same holders in a different order (N4). On severity, the door refuses where the boot warns. That matches the install judge, ruling N2 ("the post-seal install judge refuses loudly") and the card.

Extensions (ruling X): `picklistExtensions[].extend` is judged with `callerPackageId: null`, which the runtime does too (`findOrphanPicklistExtensions`, `picklistContributions`, install judge `judge(ext, own, null)`). **Right.** It is pinned as a CONTROL.

Outside-dependency info notice: kept in kind for `not-found`. For `outside-closure` the new short wording ("is held only by 'S', not a declared dependency — not judged: it may come from 'X', ...") is right. For the ambiguity reasons it is wrong (row 5).

The new ≤200-char closure notice: the fixture's message is 199 characters, one under the pin. The bound is not held by construction. The message carries `where`, the list name, up to two holder ids and up to two outside ids. With HotCRM-length ids and two holders, for example `field "crm_opportunity.lead_source"` held by `'com.hotcrm.crm.core', 'com.hotcrm.crm.marketing'`, it is about 240 characters. The #22841 convention is measured on the findings the suite fires (`explain-rule-id.test.ts` `cliFindings()` fires only the `not-found` notice), and the old notice had the same unbounded shape, so this is a nit (N1).

Public surface: no export added, removed or re-typed. `PICKLIST_REFERENCE_UNKNOWN`, `PICKLIST_REFERENCE_UNVERIFIED`, `PICKLIST_RESIDUAL_UNREFERENCED`, `judgePicklistReferences`, `printPicklistReferenceNotices` and `picklistRefusalHeading` keep their signatures. No rule id, severity or `covers` moves. New imports come from `@objectstack/core` and `@objectstack/metadata-core`, both already `workspace:*` dependencies of `@objectstack/cli` (`package.json:65,74`) and both re-exported from their barrels. Text faces that move: the refusal heading (forced pin, declared), the refusal `message` and `hint` for the new arms, and the `os explain picklist-reference-unverified` paragraphs. **Right**, and declared.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/cli` is **right**. Read with `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` (`readClause2Line` / `readMetadataProtocolLine`) on both carriers:
- changeset: `{"kind":"declared","value":"no","arm":"narrowing"}` · `{"kind":"declared","value":"none"}`
- PR body: `{"kind":"declared","value":"no","arm":"narrowing"}` · `{"kind":"declared","value":"none"}`

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds: the diff widens no accept set and adds no public name. Every accept-set move in ① narrows, or adds a non-gating notice where there was silence. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no key of any schema is added, removed or re-shaped. The door now refuses references that the runtime rule shipped in E6 already refuses, and E6's own changeset declared that runtime narrowing `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: none` / `patch`. The ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is present and green (Check Changeset). `@objectstack/lint` changes (one explanation text) and is not named in the front matter. It is in the `fixed` group with `@objectstack/cli`, so it releases at the same version anyway (N6). The declaration of *what* narrows is incomplete; that is ④ F2, not a level question.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question 1 (rule id for the closure refusal).** Seat: reuse `picklist-reference-unknown`. **Concur.** The rule id names one fact (the name reaches no list from where it is written), R's sentence carries the reason, and a new id would be a new public name that the card's delta does not admit.
- **Open question 2 (`os explain` text).** Seat: widen to `rule-explanations.ts` for that entry. **Concur.** The edit stays inside the `picklist-reference-unverified` entry and moves no id, severity or `covers`. It edits two paragraphs (the first, and the fix sentence of the third) where the amendment says "(one paragraph)". Both are that entry's text, and the third-paragraph edit is the fix the first one implies, so the amendment's binding scope ("only the entry's text") holds (N6). No pinned string moved (`rule-explanations.test.ts` and `explain-rule-id.test.ts` read the id and `covers` only).
- **Open question 3 (#31841 ordering).** Seat: whichever lands second drops the "not yet wired" note. **Concur.** #31841 (open, head `0a18e768`) inserts its dated note right after the paragraph this PR rewrites. If #31841 lands second, its hunk conflicts on that paragraph and must drop the note. If this PR lands second, it must merge main and drop it. Either way the header must not keep both. Until #31841 lands, this header cites "ADR-0130's dated note under D1", which is not on `main` yet (N5). Ruling 6729820123 gave the dated note at "picklist-references.ts line 42" to child A, and the card (filed after the ruling, as the code carrier the ruling did not name) asks for the rewrite. The rewrite replaces a sentence that would otherwise be false, and "⛔ No rewrite of the ADR-0130 text" binds the ADR, not this comment. **No conflict.**
- **Dev deviations**: no assignee, no PR subscription, and the ADR-0087 marker category. **None of them is a contract concern.** The marker is the one E6 used, and its gate is green.
- **Dev out-of-scope finding**: the first boot-parity describe's CONTROL stack is now one this door refuses. **Noted, nit (N3).** The CONTROL asserts only the residual rule, so its meaning holds, but the label reads as a clean stack.
- **Unflagged, raised here**: F1 and F2 below (the ambiguity arms). Neither is escalated. Both are should-fix inside this PR's own file surface.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** It takes away no declared capability at the consumer. The sibling allowance was ADR-0130-era prose in this module's header and in the `os explain` text. Ruling N1 overruled it, and since E6 (`cc16008a`) the runtime no longer honours it: the field is served no options, its values are refused, and the install is refused. ADR-0150 D3 names `os validate` among the doors that refuse a reference R refuses. This PR makes that refusal real at the door, in R's own words, through R's own two calls. The narrowing is real and right.

Cases tried:
- **A sibling reached transitively through a declared dependency**: resolves. `packageDependencyClosure` walks `dependencies` transitively through the view's `getPackage`. Pinned (CONTROL, base → core).
- **A `sys` list**: resolves with no dependency (`kernelPackages` reads `namespace === 'sys'` from `getAllPackages`). Pinned.
- **The declaring package's own list**: step 1, whatever a sibling holds. Pinned.
- **A stack with no `packages[]`**: one body, and `packageId` is the manifest id or `'this stack'`. Every holder is the caller, so step 1 applies and nothing changes. The `id !== ''` tightening only stops `''` from being read as the stack's own id. No new pin; the existing one-package suite is green.
- **A list two packages hold**: neither declared → `outside-closure` naming both. Pinned. One declared → unique in the closure, so it resolves (correct, unpinned). Both declared → `ambiguous-in-closure`, a refusal: new, correct by D3, unpinned and undeclared (F2). With an outside dependency it becomes the info notice (F1).
- **An extension (`picklistExtensions`)**: caller-less, so one sibling holder resolves with no dependency (ruling X, pinned) and two holders refuse (F2).
- **A field on an object the package does not own (an `objectExtensions` field)**: the caller is the extending package (`judged.packageId`). That is the runtime's attribution: `auditPicklistReferences` reads `contributor.packageId` for the `extend` contributor, and `collectManifestPicklistReferences` attributes `objectExtensions` fields to the manifest that brings them. Correct, unpinned (N2).
- **Tried to break it further.** (a) A transitive outside dependency: P declares sibling D, D declares outside X, and the list sits only on sibling S. P's `outside` lists direct dependencies only, so the door refuses where the runtime would resolve if X itself depended on S. That needs a cross-artifact dependency cycle; nit (N8). (b) Duplicate body ids: the first body answers `getPackage` and the holders are de-duplicated, so `packageScopedHolderSource` cannot throw. (c) A `.custom` pair: widened by the same call the runtime makes. No must-fix found.

Findings:

- **F1 · should-fix.** `judgePicklistReferences` routes every `refused` verdict to the info notice once `judged.outside` is non-empty, including `ambiguous-in-closure` (field) and `ambiguous-in-environment` (extension). An outside dependency can only add a holder, so those references are certain refusals: the boot refuses them (`findUnresolvedPicklistReferences` / `findOrphanPicklistExtensions`), and D3 names `os validate` as a door that refuses them. Yet the notice tells the author "If one of those packages declares 'X', nothing is wrong". Send any `refused` verdict whose `reason` is not `outside-closure` to `refusals` whatever `outside` holds. `refusedReferenceNotice`'s "held by each of" branch then goes away. This is not a loosening against base (base was silent), so it is not a FAIL.
- **F2 · should-fix.** The narrowing is declared narrower than it is. The PR body's `Narrowing:` line and the changeset name only the `outside-closure` refusal. The head also newly refuses a field whose declaring package's declared closure reaches two holders, and a `picklistExtensions` target that two packages of the stack hold. Base accepted both because the name was "known". Both refusals are correct (D3, the boot), and the one-holder rule (`bare-name-one-holder.ts`: second holder refused post-seal, warned or refused at cold boot) makes them rare. Still, no test pins either arm (the PR's own ablation note shows the ambiguity refusal arising), and the changeset's sentence that an extension "still resolves against any package of the stack" is true only for a target one package holds. Name both in the `Narrowing:` line and the changeset, and pin each with a refusal case (first-party count stays 0).
- **N1 · nit.** The "≤200 characters" closure-notice pin passes at 199 on its fixture and is not a property of the code: realistic ids give about 240. Either fire the closure notice in `explain-rule-id.test.ts`'s `cliFindings()` so the #22841 convention measures it, or soften the test comment from a property to a fixture measurement.
- **N2 · nit.** No new case pins an `objectExtensions` field (a field on an object another package owns) naming a sibling's list. The attribution is right; one refusal case would lock it.
- **N3 · nit.** The first boot-parity describe's "CONTROL: a body-declared list a body field names" stack is now refused by this door as `picklist-reference-unknown`. Rename it, or declare the dependency there, so a CONTROL stays a clean stack.
- **N4 · nit.** For two or more holders, the door names candidates in body order and the boot in registration order, so the sentences can differ in order. The parity pin covers one holder only.
- **N5 · nit.** The header cites "ADR-0130's dated note under D1", which lands with #31841. That is fine under the seat's ordering ruling, but if #31841 is reworked the citation must follow it.
- **N6 · nit.** `@objectstack/lint` is not named in the changeset front matter (released anyway through the `fixed` group), and the `os explain` first paragraph omits the ambiguity refusal (F2's case).
- **N7 · nit, predates this PR.** The door's holder set (`picklistNamesOf`) ignores nested `plugins[]` lists, which the runtime's `collectManifestPicklistNames` counts. It is unchanged here, but it is the one remaining place where "the door is the runtime's resolver" is not exact.
- **N8 · nit.** `outside` is direct dependencies only (see the break attempt (a)). It is exotic, since it needs a cross-artifact dependency cycle.

No must-fix. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real and takes nothing declared away. F1 and F2 should land on this PR (both stay inside its file surface) or on a named follow-up before the epic seat closes E6's door work.
